findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prevent pre-stage pending state from deduplicating the request**

When a native automatic run is already pending before the User stage begins, this criterion allows that old state to suppress the first request for the new stage indefinitely. The next criterion chronology-binds completions, but no equivalent boundary is specified for pending-state deduplication; require and test that only pending work created after, or explicitly associated with, the current stage/request can suppress an invitation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Link the adapter to the existing reviewer-admission lane**

Leaving this card without a formal relationship makes the board treat it as an orphan even though `b0bb29f3-56d5-5c7c-9a1e-f4a1989e952f.md` already owns the canonical `.agents` gate and exact-head completed no-issues verdicts under parent `4f5cb66d-4fd2-47cf-92cc-2185b057a889`. Add the appropriate parent/dependency relationship through Rheos so the broader admission card cannot be completed independently while this required Codex-format slice remains unfinished.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Specify the parser bounds in the acceptance contract**

The criterion requires explicit bounds and rejection of oversized payloads but never states the maximum body, payload, field, or whitespace sizes. Consequently, incompatible implementations with materially different resource and compatibility behavior could all claim acceptance, and the oversized fixtures have no predetermined expected boundary. Record concrete byte/length limits in the card and contract before readiness.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Split the two format adapters before committing to three points**

The three-point estimate bundles two independently deliverable changes: the structured panel decoder integrated into status, completion, availability, and request state, and the unrelated classic-receipt wrapper hydration path. Each also carries separate law/policy/CLI fixtures plus contract and documentation work, so the current stop condition discovers an oversized story only after implementation starts. Split the classic wrapper from structured-state admission, or re-estimate the combined card during planning.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Define the missing false/true verdict**

The acceptance contract classifies `false/false`, `true/true`, and `true/false` but leaves the fourth boolean combination, `false/true`, undefined. If that combination is malformed or impossible it must be rejected explicitly; otherwise the decoder or one of its consumers can fall through to a different default, and there is no deterministic expected result for a fixture covering it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Move implementation evidence after the ready transition**

Requiring the card to remain in planning until both Rheos readiness and subsequent implementation evidence creates a sequencing deadlock: the repository process requires the lawful ready transition before RED/GREEN implementation begins. End the planning hold once the reviewed card is lawfully ready, then make implementation evidence gate the later testing/review transitions instead.
